chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The first one to belie the liar is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then it is the two (Recording) Angels who are with him. Then he (himself) knows that he is a liar.
ai.seo_question: Who is the first to know and reject a liar according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the progressive unveiling of truth, beginning with Allah’s absolute knowledge, followed by the testimony of the recording angels (Kiraman Katibin), and culminating in the liar’s internal realization of his own deceit. This hierarchy underscores the Shia theological concept that divine witness precedes human self-awareness, serving as a spiritual warning against hypocrisy. The hadith highlights the psychological and spiritual consequences of lying, where the liar ultimately becomes his own first witness against him.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Al Ahmar, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The first one to belie the liar is Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic. Then it is the two (Recording) Angels who are with him. Then he (himself) knows that he is a liar’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban al-Ahmar from Fudayl ibn Yasar from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘
The first one to rebuff the liar is Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, then the two angels who are with him, then he is the one who knows he is a liar.’”
